question.text: Per SEBI Circular SEBI/HO/IMD-I/DF6/P/CIR/2021/584 dated June 25, 2021 referenced in the chapter, the MAXIMUM leverage a Category III AIF can take via derivatives is:

answer.text: 2 times NAV (with investor consent and SEBI disclosure)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'Maximum Leverage should be 2 times of the Net Asset Value (NAV) of the Fund' with prior consent of investors and periodic disclosures to investors/SEBI. The Trap: 1x understates the cap. 3x is unauthorised. No-leverage is the Cat I/II rule (XIX-D territory). Cross-Exam Context: Cross-Exam Context: Cat I/II AIFs have ZERO leverage (XIX-A/D). Cat III's 2x cap is unique - XIX-B, XIX-C and XIX-E all test this. Manager's Pro-Tip: Breaching 2x is a reportable incident - install a pre-trade limit in the OMS that hard-blocks any order that would push calculated leverage > 1.9x; the 10% buffer handles intraday MTM slippage.
